skill.name: running-claude-code-via-litellm-copilot
skill.description: Guides an advanced setup that routes Claude Code through a local LiteLLM proxy backed by GitHub Copilot.
skill.summary: Route Claude Code through LiteLLM and GitHub Copilot with setup, verification, and troubleshooting guidance.
skill.author: xixu-me

security_audit.summary: The static findings are mostly Markdown false positives from documented commands, local URLs, and guarded settings examples rather than hidden execution. Two semantic risks remain: the workflow may conflict with provider policy, and the advanced header override section can emulate Copilot client identity.

remediation.issue: Unofficial proxy workflow may create provider policy risk.
remediation.suggestion: Add a stronger requirement to verify current GitHub, Copilot, Anthropic, and organizational policies before setup.

remediation.issue: Advanced header overrides can emulate a Copilot client identity.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the concrete spoofed header values or require explicit user-provided, policy-approved headers with a clear warning.

remediation.issue: Persistent Claude Code settings can reroute future model traffic.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit diff, a backup plan, and a rollback step before changing persistent settings.

remediation.issue: Package installation commands are part of the setup flow.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend isolated environments and official package sources before running LiteLLM installation commands.

content.user_title: Route Claude Code Through LiteLLM Copilot
content.value_statement: Claude Code users may need a local proxy path for Copilot-backed model access. This skill explains setup, verification, and troubleshooting steps.
actual_capabilities: Explains when a Claude Code to LiteLLM to Copilot proxy path is relevant.
Provides temporary shell setup guidance for Bash, Zsh, and PowerShell sessions.
Shows the expected LiteLLM model mapping pattern for GitHub Copilot provider routes.
Guides safe persistent configuration by merging Claude Code settings instead of replacing them.
Troubleshoots model-name mismatches, silent localhost traffic, and Copilot authorization failures.
Distinguishes default provider setup from advanced header override fallback guidance.
limitations: It does not decide whether the workflow is allowed by current GitHub or Anthropic terms.
It depends on LiteLLM and Copilot behavior that may change without notice.
It does not verify current Copilot model availability unless the user asks for fresh checks.
It requires user consent before persistent Claude Code configuration changes.

best_practices: Start with temporary environment variables before changing persistent Claude Code settings.
Keep the Claude Code requested model name exactly aligned with the LiteLLM model name.
Verify the full request chain with LiteLLM logs before troubleshooting advanced header behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not present the workaround as officially supported by GitHub or Anthropic.
Do not replace the entire Claude Code settings file to add this workflow.
Do not use header overrides until the default provider route has failed with clear evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill make the workflow officially supported?
faq.answer: No. It explains a local proxy workaround and tells users to review current provider terms themselves.

faq.question: Can it configure Claude Code permanently?
faq.answer: It can guide a merge-only persistent setup, but only after explicit user confirmation.

faq.question: Does the placeholder Anthropic token become a Copilot credential?
faq.answer: No. The placeholder only satisfies Claude Code local client expectations.

faq.question: Why must model names match exactly?
faq.answer: Claude Code requests the logical model name that LiteLLM exposes. Mismatches often cause model-not-found failures.

faq.question: Does the skill verify current Copilot model availability?
faq.answer: No. It explains the provider pattern and warns that model availability may change.

faq.question: When should header overrides be used?
faq.answer: Only after the default provider route reaches Copilot but still fails for a documented client-shape reason.
